凡 can express being ordinary or unremarkable, as in 平凡 へいぼん. It also has a broader general or overall association, used in 凡例 はんれい, a book's explanatory conventions or a map's legend. Do not translate every occurrence as "mediocre."

Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology: imagine the 几-shaped frame with one ordinary dot 丶 inside. This is a memory aid for the current shape, not a historical derivation or a claim about a phonetic component.
ボン
平凡 へいぼん — ordinary; unremarkable
ハン
凡例 はんれい — explanatory notes; legend
およ.そ
凡そ およそ — approximately; generally; usually written in kana
おうよ.そ
Preserved exactly from KANJIDIC2; no verified modern word example is supplied here.

凡て すべて — everything; a rare kanji spelling of the word taught under 全て

The two on-readings are selected for reading practice. The native readings remain recognition or lookup information here. In particular, the source-only おうよ.そ is not silently changed to おおよ.そ or treated as a verified word. In 凡そ and 凡て, the final そ and て are written outside the kanji.

For recognition, 凡そ corresponds to usually-kana およそ. The rare spelling 凡て corresponds to 全て すべて; the pronunciation and the ordinary kana word are not thereby rare.
Read 凡例 as はんれい, not ぼんれい. The same pronunciation also belongs to 判例 (はんれい), "judicial precedent," which is a different word.
丸 concerns roundness or a circle, and 九 means nine. Compare the position of the dot and the long outer stroke rather than treating these similar shapes as interchangeable.
凹 describes a concave or sunken shape, not mediocrity.

凡例 はんれい — explanatory notes; legend

凡例 names explanatory conventions or usage notes, often at the beginning of a dictionary or another reference book. It can explain how to read entries, abbreviations or symbols. On a map or diagram, it means the legend explaining the symbols, not a legendary story.
辞書を使う前に、凡例を読んでください。 (じしょをつかうまえに、はんれいをよんでください。) — Please read the usage notes before using the dictionary.
地図の凡例で、記号の意味を確認しました。 (ちずのはんれいで、きごうのいみをかくにんしました。) — I checked the meanings of the symbols in the map's legend.
Both examples use the noun: 凡例を読む (はんれいをよむ), "read the explanatory notes," and 地図の凡例 (ちずのはんれい), "a map's legend."

凡 contributes a general or overall scope here, not a judgment of mediocrity. 例 contributes conventions or established usage, not only an individual example. Together, they concern the conventions for using or interpreting the material. The on-readings are ハン + レイ: はんれい. This association helps remember the word; it is not a historical derivation.

説明 (せつめい), "explanation," and 解説 (かいせつ), "explanation; commentary," are broader. 注 (ちゅう) is an annotation that may explain a particular passage. A 凡例 explains conventions for the work or its symbols; it need not be a separate note on each difficult word. There is no useful direct antonym.

Do not use 凡例 for every introductory paragraph, example or personal memo. A book's はじめに, "introduction; preface," may discuss its purpose without giving the usage conventions that a 凡例 provides. Context determines whether English "usage notes," "explanatory notes," "legend" or "key" fits.
The homophone 判例 (はんれい) means a judicial precedent, not a map legend. Learn the whole spelling and reading rather than choosing ボン merely because it occurs in 平凡 (へいぼん).

The word is usually written in kana. 凡そ is a recognized kanji spelling, but the practical unit to learn is the whole adverb およそ. It is not a loanword or a phrase requiring an extra particle before the number.
For recognition, 凡そ corresponds to usually-kana およそ. The rare spelling 凡て corresponds to 全て すべて; the pronunciation and the ordinary kana word are not thereby rare.
全 contributes wholeness or entirety. It writes the native word すべて with て as okurigana. JMdict marks the word as usually written in kana, so すべて is an important spelling to recognize too.
全て すべて — everything; usually すべて
JMdict also records 凡て (すべて) as a rare kanji spelling. That spelling qualification does not make the pronunciation すべて rare.
